environment.description: Same EC2 instance and application code deployed behind Amazon API Gateway (REST API type) with a request validator attached to the POST /api/v1/invoice/parse method. The validator has 'validateRequestBody' set to true with a JSON-to-XML model schema (Model name: InvoiceSchema) that defines the expected structure using a content-type mapping of 'application/xml' to an XML Schema (XSD) specifying only the elements invoiceId, amount, currency, vendorName, description with simple types (xs:string, xs:decimal). The API Gateway integration uses VPC Link to the private EC2 instance. Note: API Gateway request validation performs structural schema matching on the raw body BEFORE forwarding — payloads containing DOCTYPE declarations, ENTITY definitions, processing instructions, or CDATA sections that don't conform to the declared XSD element structure are rejected with 400 at the gateway layer. The gateway's built-in XML body validation rejects any document whose root element or child structure deviates from the model, but it specifically does NOT use an XML parser itself — it performs regex-based structural pre-validation per AWS internal implementation for content-type application/xml models.

config.model_schema: XSD with root element <invoice> containing only invoiceId(string), amount(decimal), currency(string), vendorName(string), description(string)
config.note: API Gateway XML model validation uses structural pattern matching that rejects DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations as schema-non-conformant
